# OfflineShelf

> OfflineShelf builds Wikipedia reading lists for places without internet: schools, libraries and clinics. You build a list from a category, a Wikidata SPARQL query, pasted titles or the most-read articles, combine lists with set operations, rebuild them monthly and export them (TSV, static HTML, and later ZIM for Kiwix). Open source (MIT), self-hostable, launching February 2027 at https://offlineshelf.ahmershah.dev.

OfflineShelf stores article titles and IDs, never article text. Text is fetched from Wikimedia only while an export is written, and every export carries the CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution. It is an independent project, not affiliated with the Wikimedia Foundation.

## Pages

- [Home](https://offlineshelf.ahmershah.dev/): what OfflineShelf does, the four builders, combinations, rebuilds, exports and FAQ
- [How it works](https://offlineshelf.ahmershah.dev/how-it-works): build pipeline, limits and API endpoints
- [Privacy](https://offlineshelf.ahmershah.dev/privacy): what is stored and the single cookie

## Developers

- [Source code](https://github.com/ahmershahdev/offlineshelf): Python (Flask, SQLAlchemy, RQ), MariaDB, Redis, React
- [OpenAPI schema](https://github.com/ahmershahdev/offlineshelf/blob/main/docs/openapi.yaml): the JSON API under /api/v1
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/ahmershahdev/offlineshelf/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md): milestones M1 to M6
